entries.sense_en: to pierce or wound with a horn or tusk

synonyms.nuance: Uses a knife or pointed tool; gore is only for animals with horns or tusks.
synonyms.example: He stabbed the meat with a fork.

synonyms.nuance: General: make a hole through something; does not say what does it.
Stronger: pushed onto a long pointed object and held there.
synonyms.example: The knight impaled the target on his lance.

entries.sense_en: to throw a person or thing up or aside with a sudden movement of the head or horns

synonyms.nuance: Throw hard and carelessly, often in anger or haste.
synonyms.example: She flung her coat on the chair.

synonyms.nuance: Throw with great force over a distance; stronger than toss.
synonyms.example: He hurled the stone into the river.

synonyms.nuance: Throw gently in a high curve; toss is looser and can be careless.
synonyms.example: lob a ball over the net

entries.tip_ko: '토스'는 가볍게 던진다는 느낌이지만, 소·물소가 사람을 toss하면 크게 내동댕이치는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: to greet someone warmly and call them by a name

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, everyday word for saying hello.
synonyms.example: He greeted the guests at the door.

synonyms.nuance: Adds warmth: you are glad the person has come.
Formal or military: a gesture or word of respect.

entries.modern: "hail them as Sister and Brother" → "greet them as sister and brother"

entries.sense_en: a short saying that gives a rule for how to behave

synonyms.nuance: Old, popular saying passed down by everyone; a maxim can come from one author.
Plainest word; no sense of moral rule.
synonyms.example: As the saying goes, time is money.

synonyms.nuance: Formal: a well-known saying that has been true for a long time.

entries.sense_en: the hidden home of a wild animal

synonyms.nuance: Similar, but often a cave or hole where animals sleep or raise young.
A hole dug in the ground by small animals like rabbits.
Built by birds and insects; a lair is a hollow or cave used by larger animals.

entries.sense_en: to move or rest in a lazy, relaxed way

synonyms.nuance: Sit or lie in a loose, limp way, often looking lazy or tired.
Spend time doing nothing on purpose, for pleasure.
Critical: waste time when you should be working.

entries.sense_en: to say aloud something learned by heart

synonyms.nuance: Say again; nothing about memorizing or performing.
Speak in a grand, dramatic way, like an orator.
synonyms.example: He declaimed the poem to the crowd.

synonyms.nuance: Tell what happened in your own words; recite is word-for-word.

entries.sense_en: someone or something that enters a place where it is not wanted

synonyms.nuance: Legal word: someone on private land without permission.
Stronger: enters by force, often in large numbers, to take over.
Someone who does not belong to a group; not necessarily hostile.
synonyms.example: He felt like an outsider at the party.

entries.sense_en: from memory, word for word

synonyms.nuance: Plain description: without looking at a text.
synonyms.example: She drew the map from memory.

synonyms.nuance: Verb for the learning process; 'by heart' describes the result.
British informal version of the same phrase.
synonyms.example: I know it off by heart.

entries.sense_en: to hit lightly with the open hand

synonyms.nuance: Flat hand, making a sharp sound; can be angrier than cuff.
Informal; hit with the palm, often as punishment.
British: a quick light blow, usually on the head.

entries.sense_en: old form of "do you know"

synonyms.nuance: Modern standard form.
Another old form, used without 'dost'.

entries.tip_ko: thou(너), thy(너의), thee(너를), dost(do), hast(have)는 옛 2인칭 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: a sharp, curved claw of a hunting animal

synonyms.nuance: Any pointed nail on an animal's foot; talon is stronger, for hunters.
Flat and blunt, as on human fingers; not a weapon.

entries.sense_en: silent and bad-tempered, showing you are angry or unhappy

synonyms.nuance: Similar but more childish: refusing to talk because you did not get your way.
Mood changes often; sullen is a steady bad mood.
synonyms.example: He gets moody when he is tired.

synonyms.nuance: Sad and quiet, not necessarily angry.
synonyms.example: They looked glum after the loss.

entries.sense_en: angry because something seems unfair or insulting

synonyms.nuance: General anger; does not need a feeling of being wronged.
synonyms.example: He was angry about the noise.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger: shocked and furious at something very wrong.
synonyms.example: Fans were outraged by the decision.

synonyms.nuance: Bitter feeling that lasts a long time.
synonyms.example: She felt resentful of her boss.

entries.sense_en: to finish speaking or a piece of talk

synonyms.nuance: Formal: bring a speech or meeting to its end.
synonyms.example: He concluded his speech with a joke.

synonyms.nuance: Plain word: stop doing something.
End neatly with a final touch.
synonyms.example: We rounded off the evening with coffee.

entries.tip_ko: wind /waɪnd/는 '바람 wind /wɪnd/'와 발음이 다릅니다. wound /waʊnd/는 '상처 wound /wuːnd/'와도 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: a foolish idea or action

synonyms.nuance: General quality of being silly, with no sense of a specific idea.
Stronger: something so unwise it seems crazy.
synonyms.example: It would be madness to go alone.

synonyms.nuance: Blunt and insulting: lack of intelligence.

entries.sense_en: a hard green stone used for jewelry and carvings

synonyms.nuance: A different, brighter and more valuable green gem.
General word for any precious stone.

entries.sense_en: past tense of bid: told or invited someone to do something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; neutral in force.
synonyms.example: She asked me to come again.

synonyms.nuance: Polite offer to come to an event or place.
A strong order from someone in authority.
synonyms.example: The captain commanded them to stop.

entries.modern: "bade me come again" → "told me to come again"
entries.tip_ko: bade는 /bæd/(bad와 같은 소리) 또는 /beɪd/로 읽습니다. 이 뜻의 bid는 bid-bade-bidden으로 변합니다.

entries.sense_en: people driven out of a group and not accepted by it

synonyms.nuance: Just does not belong; not necessarily pushed out.
Forced to leave one's country, often for political reasons.
synonyms.example: He lived as an exile in Paris.

synonyms.nuance: Formal, stronger: someone despised by everyone.

entries.sense_en: to hear words by accident or secretly, when not meant for you

synonyms.nuance: Listen on purpose to a private talk; overhear can be by chance.
Manage to hear part of something.

entries.sense_en: to talk proudly about what you have or can do

synonyms.nuance: Informal and slightly more childish than boast.
synonyms.example: He bragged about his new car.

synonyms.nuance: Act (not only talk) to impress people.
synonyms.example: She likes to show off her skills.

synonyms.nuance: Walk or act with proud, confident manner.

entries.sense_en: not feeling ashamed of doing wrong or rude things

synonyms.nuance: Bold and open about wrongdoing; often sounds impressive and rude at once.
Obvious, with no attempt to hide a lie or theft.
Neutral: not embarrassed; not always about bad behavior.

entries.sense_en: disgusting dirt

synonyms.nuance: Ordinary earth or dust; not always disgusting.
A layer of dirt that sticks to a surface.
Informal: wet, sticky mud or animal waste.

entries.sense_en: to fall in scattered drops or small pieces

synonyms.nuance: Bigger movement of liquid, in a wide burst.
Scattered on purpose, lightly.
Spread widely; any kind of things.

entries.sense_en: to hurt or annoy someone again and again for fun

synonyms.nuance: Playful or unkind joking; much milder.
Use power to frighten weaker people, again and again.
Stronger: cause severe pain on purpose.

entries.tip_ko: 동사는 torMENT, 명사는 TORment로 강세가 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: to settle a problem by accepting something less than you wanted

synonyms.nuance: End an argument or matter; does not say both sides give way.
Informal idiom: each side gives up half.
synonyms.example: Let's meet halfway on the price.

synonyms.nuance: One side gives up completely.
synonyms.example: He gave way to her demands.

entries.tip_ko: 'compromised things by making up a saying'에서는 '어물쩍 타협하다'의 뉘앙스가 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: to pass strips over and under each other to make a solid piece

synonyms.nuance: Twist three or more strands together, like hair or rope.
Make cloth with needles from one long thread.
British word for braid.

entries.sense_en: to want what another person has

synonyms.nuance: Stronger, with fear or anger about losing what one has; envy is wanting what others have.
synonyms.example: He is jealous of his brother.

synonyms.nuance: Formal or biblical: want something strongly, often what belongs to another.
Positive: respect, with no wish to take it.

entries.sense_en: feeling dizzy, as if the head is spinning

synonyms.nuance: Most common word for the spinning feeling.
synonyms.example: I felt dizzy on the ferris wheel.

synonyms.nuance: Feeling faint, weak, not spinning.
synonyms.example: She felt light-headed after standing up.

synonyms.nuance: About to lose consciousness.
synonyms.example: He felt faint in the heat.

entries.sense_en: to feel extreme fear or shock for a moment

synonyms.nuance: The usual English form of this idiom.
synonyms.example: My heart was in my mouth as the plane shook.

synonyms.nuance: Be startled suddenly, more sudden than long fear.
synonyms.example: The noise made me jump out of my skin.

synonyms.nuance: Nervous for a longer time, not just a moment.
synonyms.example: She was on edge all day.

entries.modern: Kipling's "heart between his teeth" → "heart in his mouth"

entries.sense_en: a group that goes with someone, to guard or guide them

synonyms.nuance: Protects; an escort also accompanies.
One person hired to protect another.
A friendly person who goes with you, not for protection.

entries.tip_ko: 명사는 ESCort, 동사는 esCORT 로 강세가 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: to hit with a quick, sharp, whipping movement

synonyms.nuance: Strike with a whip or something flexible; lash is faster.
Flat hand blow; not whipping.
Hit again and again with force.

entries.sense_en: cleverness in getting what you want, often by trickery

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned: skill in deceiving.
synonyms.example: He won by craft, not strength.

synonyms.nuance: Literary: sly cleverness, hidden tricks.
Neutral, positive: quick intelligence, without trickery.

entries.tip_ko: cunning은 '커닝(부정행위)'과 뜻이 다릅니다. 시험 커닝은 cheating.

entries.sense_en: a soft, quiet laugh

synonyms.nuance: High, silly laugh, often nervous.
Happy, snorting laugh with pleasure.
Sly, half-hidden laugh at someone.

entries.sense_en: a young bird that has just learned to fly; here, someone young and weak
entries.sense_ko: 갓 날기 시작한 새끼 새; 여기서는 어리고 약한 존재

synonyms.nuance: Any baby bird, including those too young to fly.
A young bird still in the nest.
Figurative: a beginner in any activity.

entries.sense_en: having nothing to do; here, doing something just because you are bored

synonyms.nuance: Unwillingness to work; idleness can be just having nothing to do.
Feeling of being uninterested.
Formal: not doing anything.

entries.sense_en: the state of staying alone in a quiet, hidden place, away from others

synonyms.nuance: Being kept apart from others; formal.
A quiet place to rest and get away.
Being alone, often by choice and peaceful.

entries.sense_en: marked with patches of different colors

synonyms.nuance: Round marks; mottled has uneven patches.
Many tiny dots.
Uneven, in patches; may not have several colors.

entries.sense_en: the back legs and hips of an animal, on which it sits

synonyms.nuance: Technical: the whole back part of a four-legged animal.
Just the rear end above the tail.

entries.sense_en: trees and their wood

synonyms.nuance: Most general word for material from trees.
American: cut wood ready for building.
Living plants, not the material.

entries.sense_en: careful and watchful because of possible danger

synonyms.nuance: Careful to avoid risk; positive.
Thinks something is wrong or someone is dishonest.
Fully awake and ready to act.

entries.tip_ko: 'be wary of ~'로 씁니다. weary(지친)와 혼동 주의.

entries.sense_en: in a polite, respectful way

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; good manners.
Shows respect for the person's rank.
synonyms.example: She spoke respectfully to the judge.

synonyms.nuance: Kind and elegant, often from a higher position.

entries.sense_en: not proud; not thinking you are better than others

synonyms.nuance: Does not boast about one's success; humble sees oneself as low.
synonyms.example: He is modest about his talent.

synonyms.nuance: Too gentle and quiet, easily pushed around.
Quietly ordinary; no show.

entries.sense_en: too bold and confident, doing what you have no right to do

synonyms.nuance: Proud, thinking oneself better than others.
Informal: annoyingly sure of oneself.
Milder: too bold in a social way.
synonyms.example: It was rather forward of him.

entries.sense_en: to what place; where

synonyms.nuance: Modern word; covers both place and direction.
Any place at all.

entries.sense_en: the leaves of trees and plants

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for each leaf.
Green plants seen as decoration.
synonyms.example: The room was full of greenery.

synonyms.nuance: All plant life in an area, not only leaves.

entries.sense_en: a long time with very little rain

synonyms.nuance: Shorter, milder period without rain.
Lack of food, often caused by drought.

entries.sense_en: side by side, level with

synonyms.nuance: Beside something; can be moving or still.
Plain description.
At the same point in a race or line.
synonyms.example: He drew level with the leader.

entries.tip_ko: 'keep abreast of the news'처럼 '~에 뒤처지지 않다'로도 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a smooth, quick running pace, slower than a gallop

synonyms.nuance: Slower, bouncy pace.
synonyms.example: The horse broke into a trot.

synonyms.nuance: Fastest pace.
Long, easy strides.
synonyms.example: The wolf loped across the field.

entries.sense_en: a raised road or path, often paved with stone

synonyms.nuance: General word.
Narrow route for walkers.
Crosses over a river or gap.

entries.sense_en: the top of a castle wall, with gaps for defenders to shoot through

synonyms.nuance: Whole defensive wall or bank.
Low wall at the edge of a roof or bridge.

entries.sense_en: a plant that grows along walls or the ground

synonyms.nuance: Woody climbing plant, like grape vines.
Specific evergreen climber.
Plant that climbs a support.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 구어의 creeper(소름 끼치는 사람)와는 다른 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: delicate stone patterns of crossing lines in a window or screen

synonyms.nuance: Crossed strips forming a grid, often simple.
Very fine ornament, usually of metal wire.
Pattern like lace.

entries.sense_en: decorative pattern cut or carved into a thin surface

synonyms.nuance: Crossing strips, forming a grid.
Any decoration with holes cut through.

entries.sense_en: the wide flap of skin around a cobra's neck, spread when it is angry

synonyms.nuance: A monk's loose hood; the cobra's hood is named for this kind of head covering.
Plain body part; hood means the neck skin when it is spread wide.

entries.tip_ko: 'Down hoods all!'은 '모두 펼친 목 두건을 접어라', 즉 공격 자세를 풀라는 명령입니다.

entries.sense_en: to run away in fear

synonyms.nuance: Plain description.
Formal: escape from danger.
Draw back, often in an orderly way.

entries.sense_en: a heavy beam swung to break down walls or gates

synonyms.nuance: Big hammer used by hand.
Short form; also a male sheep.

entries.sense_en: crouching low and shaking in fear

synonyms.nuance: Shrink back in fear or shame; can be mental.
A quick small movement from pain or shock.
Bend low; not always from fear.

entries.sense_en: laughing at someone to show they are worthless

synonyms.nuance: Making fun in a public, cruel way.
Copying or teasing someone to laugh at them.
Deep feeling that someone is unworthy.

entries.sense_en: loud, confused noise of many voices

synonyms.nuance: Continuous loud, unpleasant noise.
Angry shouting, often from a crowd.
Informal: annoying loud noise.

entries.sense_en: grabbed and held tightly

synonyms.nuance: Grab suddenly and firmly.
Informal: take quickly.
Hold firmly; gentler than seize.

entries.sense_en: to accept a sensible argument and change your mind

synonyms.nuance: Change one's mind, often after persuasion.
synonyms.example: She will come round in time.

synonyms.nuance: Almost the same, often in a warning.
Stop resisting, not always because it is sensible.

entries.tip_ko: 'make someone see reason'은 '~를 설득해서 이성적으로 만들다'.

entries.sense_en: the power to hold someone helpless by staring, like a spell

synonyms.nuance: Magic spell or charm.
Deliberate trance made by a hypnotist.
Attraction that pulls people; gentler.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 '큰 흥미'를 뜻하지만, 여기서는 옛 뜻(홀림)입니다.

entries.sense_en: to change something without right, especially to spoil or break it

synonyms.nuance: Interfere in someone's affairs.
General: get in the way.
Informal: touch or play with idly.

entries.sense_en: a chain or garland hanging in a curve

synonyms.nuance: Ring or chain of flowers or leaves.
Circle of flowers or leaves.
Links joined in a line, of any material.

entries.sense_en: from here; away from this place

synonyms.nuance: Modern, plain word for leaving.
Modern meaning: as a result.
